evals.prompt: I have a Next.js app with shadcn/ui (base-nova). Add a small synth panel: an oscillator I can start and stop, a filter cutoff knob, a resonance knob and an output volume fader in dB.
evals.expected_output: Registry Knob and Fader installed with npx shadcn@latest add @audio-ui/..., wired to Web Audio nodes with ramped parameters, a lazily created AudioContext resumed in the start click.
expectations: Installs the controls from the registry with `shadcn@latest add @audio-ui/knob` and `@audio-ui/fader` (or the project's package runner), not a hand-written slider
The cutoff knob uses scale="log" with a positive min (e.g. 20 to 20000)
Parameters are set with setTargetAtTime (or another ramp), never by assigning .value from onValueChange
The fader value in dB is converted to linear gain (10 ** (db / 20)) before reaching the GainNode
The AudioContext is created lazily on the client and resume() is called inside the click handler that starts sound
Every control has an aria-label or a visible label
The file that uses hooks or the browser starts with "use client"
Sets step and largeStep to fit the dB, Hz and resonance ranges, not the 0 to 100 defaults
Prints units with formatValue (or the label), never with an Intl unit such as hertz or decibel
Imports the installed components from the path the CLI wrote (components/audio-ui/<name>)
Keeps the loudest case under full scale: voice gain well below 1, resonance capped, and a master volume that stops at 0 dB

evals.prompt: Show the live level of the microphone as a stereo meter with peak hold.
evals.expected_output: A Meter fed by a source built with createSource and updated in requestAnimationFrame from AnalyserNodes, with getUserMedia behind a click.
expectations: Levels reach the Meter through its `source` prop, built with createSource (or another getSnapshot/subscribe object), not through useState updated every frame
Levels are computed from AnalyserNode data (RMS in dB) in a requestAnimationFrame loop that is cancelled on cleanup
Stereo uses one analyser per channel (e.g. via ChannelSplitterNode)
Peak hold is computed by the app and published as `peaks`
getUserMedia is started from a user action, not on mount
Does not install a non-existent `@audio-ui/use-audio-levels` item
Imports the installed Meter from the path the CLI wrote (components/audio-ui/meter)
Turns off the browser's voice processing (echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, autoGainControl) so the meter shows the raw signal
A mono microphone still moves both bars (up-mixed to two channels), and the analysers are never connected to the destination

evals.prompt: Build a 16-step drum sequencer with kick, snare and hat rows, a tempo control and play/stop.
evals.expected_output: Sequencer from the registry, sounds scheduled at AudioContext time through use-transport-clock, playhead from getPosition via a source.
expectations: Uses the audio/ui Sequencer (registry or @audio-ui/react), not a grid of buttons
Steps are scheduled on the audio clock (use-transport-clock onStep time, or an equivalent look-ahead), not with setInterval/setTimeout triggering sounds immediately
Each sound starts at the scheduled `time` (e.g. osc.start(time))
Stop or seek silences sound already scheduled ahead (onReset or equivalent)
The moving playhead does not re-render React every frame
The AudioContext is resumed inside the Play click handler, not on mount
The summed voices have headroom: a master gain below 1, or an equivalent
The grid and the controls have accessible names

evals.prompt: My app has its own CSS design system and no Tailwind or shadcn. I need a rotary knob for pan that matches our styles.
evals.expected_output: Knob primitive from @audio-ui/react/knob assembled from its parts, styled via className functions / data attributes, anchor={0}, focus-visible styles.
expectations: Installs @audio-ui/react and imports Knob (ideally from the @audio-ui/react/knob entry), not the shadcn registry
Assembles the documented parts (Root, Control, Track, Indicator, Thumb...)
Styles state through className/style functions or data-* attributes (e.g. data-dragging), not by tracking pointer state manually
Uses anchor={0} with min -1 and max 1 for pan
Keeps Knob.Thumb (the focusable part) and styles :focus-visible
Gives the knob an accessible name
Sets step and largeStep to fit the -1 to 1 range (for example step 0.01 and largeStep 0.1), not the 0 to 100 defaults

evals.prompt: Add a chat box next to my piano roll so I can type things like 'write a walking bassline in C minor' and 'transpose it up an octave'. I use the Vercel AI SDK.
evals.expected_output: createPianoRollTools from @audio-ui/piano-roll-tools wired as AI SDK tools that update the same controlled notes state; current notes passed to the model.
expectations: Installs or uses @audio-ui/piano-roll-tools (createPianoRollTools) instead of inventing a free-form JSON protocol
Configures the tools from the roll's own range and grid, not hard-coded values unrelated to the component
Tool execute functions update the same React state the PianoRoll is controlled by (apply(prev, args)), not the DOM
Gives the model the current notes (prompt or read tool)
The person can still edit the roll by hand and undo
Declares the tools on the server without execute and runs each call in the browser on the roll's state (onToolCall plus addToolOutput), since the model call is server-side
Records one undo step per model edit, kept outside any setState updater

evals.prompt: Every time I drag the volume fader my app saves the preset to the server and the network tab explodes. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Moves the save to onValueCommitted, keeps audio updates on onValueChange.
expectations: Moves the save/network call to onValueCommitted
Keeps the audio/state update on onValueChange
Does not add a debounce as the main fix

evals.prompt: My app is in Vue 3 (no React). I want a rotary knob for filter cutoff, keyboard accessible, with our own CSS.
evals.expected_output: A Vue composable over createKnobController from @audio-ui/core/knob: created once, setOptions plus resync on change, drawn from getSnapshot, a hidden range input wired to keyDown and type, listeners removed on dispose.
expectations: Uses @audio-ui/core (createKnobController from @audio-ui/core/knob), not @audio-ui/react or the shadcn registry
Creates the controller once per component, not in a computed or on every option change
Calls setOptions with the full options when they change and resyncs the snapshot afterwards
Draws rotation and text from getSnapshot() (angle, formatted), not from its own angle math
Keeps a visually hidden input type=range with an accessible name, keydown routed to knob.keyDown (preventDefault when it returns true) and input routed to knob.type
Removes the subscription and the wheel listener on unmount (onScopeDispose or onUnmounted)
Uses scale: "log" with a positive min for the cutoff
Calls setOptions with all the options before the first draw, so the log scale applies from the start
Prepares the pointer before press: primary button only, preventDefault, focuses the hidden input, touch-action none

evals.prompt: Add a guitar tuner to my Next.js app: listen to the microphone and show the note and how many cents sharp or flat it is.
evals.expected_output: The registry Tuner with use-microphone and use-pitch: the microphone started from a click, raw signal, an analyser never connected to the speakers, a period search for the pitch, and a live source, not state per frame.
expectations: Installs `@audio-ui/tuner`, `@audio-ui/use-microphone` and `@audio-ui/use-pitch` from the registry (or uses `detectPitch` and `nearestNote` from `@audio-ui/core/pitch`), not a hand-written pitch detector
Starts the microphone from a user gesture (a click), so the permission prompt and the context resume have one
Takes the raw microphone signal: echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain are off
Does not connect the analyser to `ctx.destination`, so the microphone is not played back
Finds the pitch from the time-domain samples (a period search such as YIN), not from the loudest FFT bin, which reads a harmonic
Gives the display a live source (what `usePitch` returns), not `setState` on every reading
Releases the microphone's tracks when listening stops or the component unmounts

evals.prompt: I want to play my synth from a USB MIDI keyboard. Harder keys should be louder, and the pitch wheel should bend the notes.
evals.expected_output: use-midi-input connected from a button click, velocity from 0 to 1 scaling the voice gain, a note on with velocity 0 treated as a release, pitch bend in semitones, and the AudioContext resumed because MIDI is not a gesture.
expectations: Uses `useMidiInput` (registry `@audio-ui/use-midi-input`) or `createMidiInput` and `parseMidiMessage` from `@audio-ui/core/midi`, not its own `onmidimessage` handlers on each component
Asks for MIDI access from a click (a connect button such as `MidiConnectControl`), never on mount
Scales a voice's gain by the note's velocity from 0 to 1, not a fixed gain
Treats a note on with velocity 0 as a note off
Applies the pitch bend as a number of semitones to the sounding voices (a bend range of 2 by default), with a ramp
Resumes a suspended AudioContext before the first note, since a MIDI message is not a user gesture for audio

evals.prompt: My equalizer plot draws a low-pass at Q 2 with a bump at the cutoff, but the sound I hear has a different bump. The plot uses a BiquadFilterNode with filter.Q.value = 2 for the audio.
evals.expected_output: Explain that a low-pass and a high-pass take Q in decibels in the Web Audio node, convert it with toWebAudioQ, draw the curve from biquadResponse, and note that a shelf ignores Q.
expectations: Says that a `lowpass` or `highpass` BiquadFilterNode reads its `Q` in decibels, so `Q.value = 2` is a 2 dB resonance, not a linear Q of 2
Converts with `toWebAudioQ` from `@audio-ui/core/analysis` (20 * log10 of the linear Q), or sets Q to about 6.02 dB for a linear Q of 2
Draws the curve with `biquadResponse` or `eqResponse` from `@audio-ui/core/analysis` rather than a hand-made formula, so the plot equals `getFrequencyResponse`
Mentions that a shelf's Q is ignored by the node
Sets parameters on the node with `setTargetAtTime`, not `.value =`, while it plays

evals.prompt: I am building a small DAW. Add a compressor to a track: my project already has its own audio engine and stores each effect's settings in the project file. An AI assistant should also be able to change its settings from chat.
evals.expected_output: The compressor as a device: defineDevice's state stored in the project, the controlled panel, the host's own engine driven through a DeviceBinding or compressorSettings, and deviceTools for the assistant, with a device id stored rather than the panel.
expectations: Keeps the compressor's settings as a plain state object (the `compressorDevice` state of `@audio-ui/core/device`) in the project, not inside a component's `useState` with audio nodes
Stores the device's `id` (`audioui.compressor`) and its state in the project file, and repairs a loaded state with `device.sanitize`
Uses the controlled panel (`CompressorPanel` or `DevicePanel`) with `value` and `onValueChange`, not a component that owns its state
Drives the project's own engine from the state (a `DeviceBinding` with `update(state)` and `dispose()`, or the numbers of `compressorSettings`), instead of the Web Audio engine of the registry
Gives the assistant `deviceTools(compressorDevice)` (or `describe()` and `apply`) with their JSON Schema input, not a hand-written prompt of parameter names
Feeds the tool's returned `state` back to the project and its `summary` back to the model, and does not parse prose from the model
Does not apply a model's value as is: it goes through the device, which clamps it and refuses an unknown or mistyped parameter

evals.prompt: My chat assistant should be able to play the Pocket Synth: when I say 'play an A, then a lower one', it should sound. The synth is already on the page.
evals.expected_output: The synth as an instrument device: deviceTools gives a play tool from the device's note, its result's note and duration go to the engine through playNote, with values brought into range.
expectations: Uses `deviceTools(pocketSynthDevice)` and its third tool, `audioui_pocket_synth_play`, with its JSON Schema input, instead of a hand-written prompt of notes
Gives the result's `note` and `duration` to the engine with `playNote(engine, note, seconds)` or `noteOn` then `noteOff`, instead of parsing the model's prose
Gives the tool's `summary` back to the model, and lets the device bring a pitch outside the instrument's range into range instead of passing it on
Does not rebuild the synth: the engine's `noteOn` and `noteOff` are used as the registry gives them
